items.explanation: 71-year-old man (dob 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-08-22 cardiac surgery admission (Condition 7010d0e5) and carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note since, including the most recent visit 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference 174a63cd). No anticoagulant is current: the only active outpatient order/medication list entry is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, and no warfarin or DOAC order covers 2026-09-24. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery = vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS class 1, score >=2 in men). Needs prescriber review to start anticoagulation; prior post-procedural hemorrhage (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an absolute contraindication.

On citalopram 40 mg daily continuously since 2023-10-02 (current order 7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 71 bpm with QT 506-514 ms and Bazett QTc 547-555 ms (>=500 ms), versus QTc 446 ms on the previous tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). Latest potassium 4.5 mmol/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg exceeds the dose recommended for QT safety in many patients; prescriber review of the dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; it first appears on that visit's medication list and no earlier citalopram order exists). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (sinus rhythm, 81 bpm, QTc 387 ms) - obtained 5 days after the start, so the requirement is met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; earlier amiodarone exposure was inpatient in January 2025 and had ended). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the original memo applies: ECG due within 30 days, by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24 (14 days), so the requirement is met - although that ECG shows QTc 535 ms, which is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order cbe91d0f, the first escitalopram order in the chart). Started before 2026-03-01, so the 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QTc about 474 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold), so the requirement is met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order 88943096, first escitalopram order in the chart). Start is after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not satisfied in time and remains overdue as of 2026-09-24. For information, that late tracing showed sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QTc 383 ms (and a limb-lead reversal pattern).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a; it first appears on that visit's medication list - the only earlier exposure was a brief inpatient course ending 2026-01-01). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and there is no result or report of an outside tracing, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a; the only earlier exposure was inpatient in 2024). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264; it first appears on that visit's medication list, earlier haloperidol having been inpatient in Feb-Mar 2025). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928, sinus 58 bpm, QTc 416 ms), but the deadline is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change, so the requirement is met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 (DocumentReference 9579a764, L. Nguyen PharmD): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist acting under the standing order, so an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is INR(PT) 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on warfarin plus amiodarone (an interacting drug).

71-year-old woman (dob 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction (Condition 66dd1300; same admission also coded cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia and ataxia following infarction). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). No anticoagulant has ever been started: current outpatient orders as of 2026-09-24 are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID and famotidine only, and the clinic medication lists through 2026-07-10 contain no warfarin or DOAC. Anticoagulation is class 1 recommended for AF with prior stroke; needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia and documented falls from 2025-03 should be considered but do not preclude treatment). Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

80-year-old woman (dob 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every Cardiology Clinic note from 2025-09-12 through the most recent visit 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference 5116e8ae ... a41e9ebb), and continuous monitored AF during the 2025-01-11 to 2025-01-20 admission (Heart Rhythm observations dee1f439 through 2558914f, 2025-01-17 to 2025-01-20). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria and hemiparesis 2, old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF; oral anticoagulation is class 1 recommended and needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-06-10 (96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.14 and 0.04) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 and 136 bpm (RR 348-650 ms). Monitored Heart Rhythm entries from the same admission (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12) also record AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 2024-05-14 (current order 8de890c6, 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 489-494 ms and Bazett QTc 522 ms (>=500 ms), an increase of >150 ms from the previous ECG (100065910, QTc 360 ms). The 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable', which the measurement does not support. Latest electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23). Per the QT monitoring memo this requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is also warranted since the last tracing is nearly 3 years old.

79-year-old man with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily (started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit, current order 1014aca9 through 2027-01-05) plus warfarin. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QT 527-531 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms (>=500 ms), up 114 ms from the previous ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07, QTc 421 ms). Latest potassium 4.4 mmol/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal. Requires prescriber review of amiodarone dose/continuation and a repeat ECG.

95-year-old woman with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily continuously since 2022-03-01 (current order c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05) together with warfarin. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 59-64 bpm with sinus bradycardia and a premature couplet, QT 562 ms and Bazett QTc 560 ms (582 ms if the mean RR is used), up about 100 ms from the AF tracing 3 weeks earlier (100867733, QTc 451 ms). Latest potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; no ECG has been recorded since 2022 despite continued amiodarone, so a repeat tracing with electrolytes is needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with a consistent P wave before every QRS (beat-to-beat P correlation 0.97), PR 185 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 330 ms giving Bazett QTc 387 ms, frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison; the 2026-03-07 clinic note describing sinus rhythm agrees with the tracing despite his history of atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm with a consistent P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.95), PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 335-367 ms with Bazett QTc 439-482 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with an inverted T wave ending about 265 ms after QRS onset, QTc about 414 ms; the QTc difference is well under 60 ms and rhythm and conduction are unchanged. No atrial fibrillation is captured on either tracing despite the note history of paroxysmal AF.

Sinus tachycardia at 108-109 bpm, regular, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 338 ms with Bazett QTc 457 ms (mildly prolonged, partly an artefact of Bazett correction at this rate), axis about +41 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.04), irregularly irregular RR 348-650 ms, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm. QRS 96 ms, QT 282-291 ms with Bazett QTc about 424-437 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR is not measurable. The prior ECG earlier the same evening (107914094, 2026-06-10 17:13) also showed atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc about 432-444 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between the two. Note that the clinic note of the same date describes 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (flagged separately).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with regular RR intervals (864-882 ms) and a low-amplitude but consistent P wave, PR about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 398-417 ms with Bazett QTc 426-446 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with QTc about 405-411 ms but showed a negative lead I with positive aVR (an extreme/reversed limb-lead pattern); the QTc change is about 20 ms, so no change flags apply.

Sinus rhythm at 97-98 bpm, PR about 108 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 306-312 ms with Bazett QTc 390-397 ms, axis about -1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 367-385 ms with Bazett QTc 402-423 ms, axis about +21 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; QTc is well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold, but this tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 (post-start ECG still outstanding).

Atrial fibrillation: P waves absent (pre-QRS correlation -0.08) with grossly irregular RR intervals (560-1164 ms) and a mean ventricular rate of about 70 bpm. QRS 84 ms, QT about 420-446 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 455 ms using the mean RR (489 ms using the median RR), axis about +29 degrees, no bundle branch block, PR not measurable. The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12, pre-operative) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 168 ms and QTc about 399-409 ms, so this tracing shows NEW_AF (post-cardiac-surgery, with monitored AF entries on 2024-11-13 to 2024-11-15). The QTc rise is 48 ms on a mean-RR basis, below the 60 ms change threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, P wave before every QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 423-433 ms with Bazett QTc 416-427 ms, axis about +60 degrees. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG the day before (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62 bpm, QTc 450 ms) is essentially unchanged (QTc difference about 35 ms). This is the most recent tracing available; haloperidol was started 2026-09-15 and the post-start ECG is not yet due.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 347-349 ms with Bazett QTc 409-412 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76-77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT about 415 ms with Bazett QTc 469 ms (borderline prolonged), axis about +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with diffusely inverted T waves and QT about 470 ms, QTc about 524 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 55 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, so no change flag is recorded.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, P wave before each QRS with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, no AV block), QRS 90 ms, QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 395 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG (106186980, 2016-09-16: sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (-6 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 54-55 bpm with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, QT 403 ms with Bazett QTc 384 ms, axis about +4 degrees. The prior ECG (103042067, 2024-11-30) was sinus rhythm at 51 bpm with PR about 186-198 ms and QTc 365-367 ms; the QTc change is under 60 ms and there was no bundle branch block then either, so no change flags apply (the PR prolongation is at most marginally new and first-degree AV block is not a listed change).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves (pre-QRS correlation -0.06), irregularly irregular RR 312-604 ms, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. QRS 100 ms, QT 265-268 ms with Bazett QTc about 415-426 ms, axis about -21 degrees, no bundle branch block, PR not measurable. The prior ECG the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with QTc about 421-424 ms, so this is NEW_AF (post-operative day 2 after cardiac surgery, with monitored AF entries 2025-09-13 to 2025-09-15). The QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 357-361 ms with Bazett QTc 395-399 ms, axis about +12 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) showed sinus rhythm at 68-70 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of 510-512 ms and QTc 542-544 ms; the QTc has fallen by nearly 150 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). The clinic note of 2026-11-23 describing sinus rhythm agrees with this tracing.
Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 178 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 387-389 ms with Bazett QTc 429-432 ms, axis about +55 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 292-294 ms with Bazett QTc 398-401 ms, axis about +34 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG (102955795, 2022-07-04: sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 394-395 ms) is unchanged. Despite a coded history of atrial flutter/fibrillation, all of this patient's tracings (2016-2023) show sinus rhythm; he remains on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one premature beat and a compensatory pause (RR 964, 986, 560, 1368, then 954-986 ms); the underlying rhythm is regular with a consistent P wave, PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block, QT 397-400 ms with Bazett QTc 403-407 ms, frontal axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation (net QRS negative in II, III and aVF). Recorded on the day of her embolic stroke admission (2025-03-14); no atrial fibrillation is captured on this 10-second tracing even though paroxysmal AF was diagnosed during that admission. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (regular RR 838-884 ms) with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS, PR about 140 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 356-360 ms with Bazett QTc 383-387 ms. The frontal axis measures about -173 degrees (extreme): lead I and II are deeply negative while aVR is positive and the precordial leads are normal, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70-71 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is prolonged at 506-514 ms with a Bazett QTc of 547-555 ms. The prior ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QT 300-304 ms and QTc 446-451 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 100 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) while on citalopram 40 mg daily; this meets the clinic threshold for prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis about +58 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are inverted in I, V5 and V6 with a low-amplitude late positive deflection; QT measures about 445-448 ms (Bazett QTc 474-478 ms) taking the end of the T wave in the lead where it is latest, and about 405 ms (QTc 432 ms) if measured on lead I alone. Either way the QTc is below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This is the ECG obtained after escitalopram was started on 2026-02-12 and is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 54-66 bpm (sinus beats at RR 1110-1160 ms) interrupted by premature beats/couplets (RR 480-660 ms); P waves are consistent before the sinus beats with PR about 174 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 395-397 ms with Bazett QTc 374-376 ms using the dominant RR, axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (108651109, 2018-12-13) was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR about 210 ms and QTc 391-394 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc are essentially unchanged (no AF on either tracing).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis about +47 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is markedly prolonged at 489-494 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 522 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms with QTc 360 ms at 75 bpm, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). The patient has been on escitalopram since 2024-05-14; this tracing is his most recent and meets the clinic threshold (QTc >= 500 ms) for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02) with a consistent low-amplitude P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.93, PR about 178 ms); no pacing spikes are present despite the pacemaker in situ. QRS 80 ms, QT 272-276 ms with Bazett QTc 416-423 ms, axis about -2 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (no P waves, RR 380-824 ms, mean 110 bpm, QTc about 436-439 ms), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing (RESOLVED_AF); the QTc change is about 20 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 100 ms (slightly wide but below the 120 ms bundle branch block threshold and without an RBBB or LBBB pattern), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 447-448 ms, axis about +34 degrees. No AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with a broad but consistent P wave; measuring from the sharp onset of the P in lead II and V1 the PR is about 165 ms (a slowly drifting baseline makes the automated estimate as long as 214 ms, but true first-degree AV block is not convincingly present). QRS 78 ms, QT 337-341 ms with Bazett QTc 414-419 ms, axis about -17 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (102616671, 2021-05-16: sinus 87 bpm, PR about 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 395-396 ms) shows no significant change.

Sinus rhythm at 59-61 bpm with a prolonged PR of about 210-212 ms (first-degree AV block) and a wide QRS of 130 ms showing a QS complex in V1-V3 with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 and no septal q waves, i.e. left bundle branch block. QT 443-453 ms with Bazett QTc 447-457 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees. The prior ECG (103686933, 2024-06-03) showed the same pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 210 ms, QRS 128 ms LBBB, QTc 450-462 ms), so there is no change: the bundle branch block is not new and the QTc is stable.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 334-335 ms with Bazett QTc 435-436 ms, axis about +47 degrees, no conduction abnormality. The prior ECG the previous day (101016166, 2025-03-18: sinus 102 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 432-436 ms) is unchanged.
Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 375 ms with Bazett QTc 392-393 ms, axis about -21 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 59-64 bpm: the dominant beats are regular (RR 970-1100 ms) with a consistent P wave and PR about 198 ms (just below the first-degree block threshold), interrupted by one premature couplet (RR 588 and 506 ms). QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about +39 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at 562 ms, Bazett QTc 560 ms (582 ms using the mean RR). The prior ECG three weeks earlier (100867733, 2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation (no P waves, RR 324-616 ms, mean 128 bpm) with QTc about 451-462 ms, so on this tracing the atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has increased by about 100 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) - she remains on amiodarone, and the QTc exceeds the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT about 338 ms (the tangent to the T wave downslope; a later low-amplitude U/P deflection should not be included) with Bazett QTc 452 ms, axis about +54 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG (107274479, 2019-07-27: sinus 75 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 389 ms, QTc 434-435 ms) shows no change in rhythm or conduction and a QTc difference under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.01) and a consistent P wave before each QRS, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 287-297 ms with Bazett QTc 408-422 ms, axis about +65 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 317-324 ms with Bazett QTc 412-421 ms, axis about +58 degrees, no conduction block. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (100 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QTc 405-416 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 168 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 419-437 ms which corrects to a Bazett QTc of 389-405 ms at this slow rate, axis about +35 degrees. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22: sinus rhythm 57 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 354-394 ms) the rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change is well under 60 ms. Despite a history of atrial fibrillation (on warfarin) this tracing shows sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm (RR 492-496 ms, regular), PR about 130 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms, QT 289-293 ms with Bazett QTc 411-417 ms. The frontal axis is rightward (net QRS negative in lead I, slightly positive in aVF, about +160 degrees). Limb-lead voltages are small and the precordial R waves are poor. The prior ECG from earlier the same day (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall late R wave in V1 (peak at 112 ms) and terminal S waves in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block, with QTc about 480-491 ms; the block is no longer present (RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK) and the QTc has fallen by about 65-75 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60), much of which follows from loss of the wide QRS.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 170 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis about +67 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is prolonged at 527-531 ms with a Bazett QTc of 535-539 ms. The previous ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) had QT 475 ms at 47-49 bpm giving QTc 421-428 ms, so the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. This is the ECG obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement and it meets the QTc >= 500 ms threshold for prescriber review.

Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.21) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 386-1070 ms, mean ventricular rate about 103 bpm. QRS 78 ms, QT 315-325 ms with Bazett QTc about 412-420 ms, frontal axis about -46 degrees (left axis deviation). 74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-06-10 (96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.14 and 0.04) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 and 136 bpm (RR 348-650 ms). Monitored Heart Rhythm entries from the same admission (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12) also record AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

71-year-old woman (dob 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction (Condition 66dd1300; same admission also coded cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia and ataxia following infarction). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). No anticoagulant has ever been started: current outpatient orders as of 2026-09-24 are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID and famotidine only, and the clinic medication lists through 2026-07-10 contain no warfarin or DOAC. Anticoagulation is class 1 recommended for AF with prior stroke; needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia and documented falls from 2025-03 should be considered but do not preclude treatment). Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

80-year-old woman (dob 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every Cardiology Clinic note from 2025-09-12 through the most recent visit 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference 5116e8ae ... a41e9ebb), and continuous monitored AF during the 2025-01-11 to 2025-01-20 admission (Heart Rhythm observations dee1f439 through 2558914f, 2025-01-17 to 2025-01-20). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria and hemiparesis 2, old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF; oral anticoagulation is class 1 recommended and needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-06-10 (96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.14 and 0.04) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 and 136 bpm (RR 348-650 ms). Monitored Heart Rhythm entries from the same admission (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12) also record AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

71-year-old woman (dob 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction (Condition 66dd1300; same admission also coded cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia and ataxia following infarction). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). No anticoagulant has ever been started: current outpatient orders as of 2026-09-24 are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID and famotidine only, and the clinic medication lists through 2026-07-10 contain no warfarin or DOAC. Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

80-year-old woman (dob 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every Cardiology Clinic note from 2025-09-12 through the most recent visit 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference 5116e8ae ... a41e9ebb), and continuous monitored AF during the 2025-01-11 to 2025-01-20 admission (Heart Rhythm observations dee1f439 through 2558914f, 2025-01-17 to 2025-01-20). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria and hemiparesis 2, old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). 74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-06-10 (96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.14 and 0.04) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 and 136 bpm (RR 348-650 ms). Monitored Heart Rhythm entries from the same admission (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12) also record AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with regular RR intervals (864-882 ms) and a low-amplitude but consistent P wave, PR about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 398-417 ms with Bazett QTc 426-446 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 97-98 bpm, PR about 108 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 306-312 ms with Bazett QTc 390-397 ms, axis about -1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 347-349 ms with Bazett QTc 409-412 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 317-324 ms with Bazett QTc 412-421 ms, axis about +58 degrees, no conduction block. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery = vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS class 1, score >=2 in men). Needs prescriber review to start anticoagulation; prior post-procedural hemorrhage (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an absolute contraindication.

On citalopram 40 mg daily continuously since 2023-10-02 (current order 7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 71 bpm with QT 506-514 ms and Bazett QTc 547-555 ms (>=500 ms), versus QTc 446 ms on the previous tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). Latest potassium 4.5 mmol/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg exceeds the dose recommended for QT safety in many patients; prescriber review of the dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order c17946a1; it first appears on that visit's medication list and no earlier citalopram order exists). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (sinus rhythm, 81 bpm, QTc 387 ms) - obtained 5 days after the start, so the requirement is met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; earlier amiodarone exposure was inpatient in January 2025 and had ended). The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the original memo applies: ECG due within 30 days, by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24 (14 days), so the requirement is met - although that ECG shows QTc 535 ms, which is flagged separately for prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order cbe91d0f, the first escitalopram order in the chart). Started before 2026-03-01, so the 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QTc about 474 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold), so the requirement is met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order 88943096, first escitalopram order in the chart). Start is after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not satisfied in time and remains overdue as of 2026-09-24. For information, that late tracing showed sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QTc 383 ms (and a limb-lead reversal pattern).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a; it first appears on that visit's medication list - the only earlier exposure was a brief inpatient course ending 2026-01-01). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and there is no result or report of an outside tracing, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a; the only earlier exposure was inpatient in 2024). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264; it first appears on that visit's medication list, earlier haloperidol having been inpatient in Feb-Mar 2025). Start after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928, sinus 58 bpm, QTc 416 ms), but the deadline is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change, so the requirement is met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 (DocumentReference 9579a764, L. Nguyen PharmD): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist acting under the standing order, so an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is INR(PT) 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on warfarin plus amiodarone (an interacting drug).

71-year-old woman (dob 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction (Condition 66dd1300; same admission also coded cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia and ataxia following infarction). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). No anticoagulant has ever been started: current outpatient orders as of 2026-09-24 are metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID and famotidine only, and the clinic medication lists through 2026-07-10 contain no warfarin or DOAC. Anticoagulation is class 1 recommended for AF with prior stroke; needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia and documented falls from 2025-03 should be considered but do not preclude treatment). Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

80-year-old woman (dob 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every Cardiology Clinic note from 2025-09-12 through the most recent visit 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference 5116e8ae ... a41e9ebb), and continuous monitored AF during the 2025-01-11 to 2025-01-20 admission (Heart Rhythm observations dee1f439 through 2558914f, 2025-01-17 to 2025-01-20). CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (acute-on-chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria and hemiparesis 2, old myocardial infarction and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF; oral anticoagulation is class 1 recommended and needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-06-10 (96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.14 and 0.04) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response at a mean rate of 134 and 136 bpm (RR 348-650 ms). Monitored Heart Rhythm entries from the same admission (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12) also record AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 2024-05-14 (current order 8de890c6, 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 489-494 ms and Bazett QTc 522 ms (>=500 ms), an increase of >150 ms from the previous ECG (100065910, QTc 360 ms). The 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable', which the measurement does not support. Latest electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23). Per the QT monitoring memo this requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is also warranted since the last tracing is nearly 3 years old.

79-year-old man with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily (started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit, current order 1014aca9 through 2027-01-05) plus warfarin. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QT 527-531 ms and Bazett QTc 535 ms (>=500 ms), up 114 ms from the previous ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07, QTc 421 ms). Latest potassium 4.4 mmol/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal. Requires prescriber review of amiodarone dose/continuation and a repeat ECG.

95-year-old woman with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily continuously since 2022-03-01 (current order c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05) together with warfarin. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 59-64 bpm with sinus bradycardia and a premature couplet, QT 562 ms and Bazett QTc 560 ms (582 ms if the mean RR is used), up about 100 ms from the AF tracing 3 weeks earlier (100867733, QTc 451 ms). Latest potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14). QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review; no ECG has been recorded since 2022 despite continued amiodarone, so a repeat tracing with electrolytes is needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with a consistent P wave before every QRS (beat-to-beat P correlation 0.97), PR 185 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 330 ms giving Bazett QTc 387 ms, frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison; the 2026-03-07 clinic note describing sinus rhythm agrees with the tracing despite his history of atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm with a consistent P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.95), PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 335-367 ms with Bazett QTc 439-482 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with an inverted T wave ending about 265 ms after QRS onset, QTc about 414 ms; the QTc difference is well under 60 ms and rhythm and conduction are unchanged. No atrial fibrillation is captured on either tracing despite the note history of paroxysmal AF.

Sinus tachycardia at 108-109 bpm, regular, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 338 ms with Bazett QTc 457 ms (mildly prolonged, partly an artefact of Bazett correction at this rate), axis about +41 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.04), irregularly irregular RR 348-650 ms, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm. QRS 96 ms, QT 282-291 ms with Bazett QTc about 424-437 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR is not measurable. The prior ECG earlier the same evening (107914094, 2026-06-10 17:13) also showed atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc about 432-444 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between the two. Note that the clinic note of the same date describes 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (flagged separately).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with regular RR intervals (864-882 ms) and a low-amplitude but consistent P wave, PR about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 398-417 ms with Bazett QTc 426-446 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with QTc about 405-411 ms but showed a negative lead I with positive aVR (an extreme/reversed limb-lead pattern); the QTc change is about 20 ms, so no change flags apply.

Sinus rhythm at 97-98 bpm, PR about 108 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 306-312 ms with Bazett QTc 390-397 ms, axis about -1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 367-385 ms with Bazett QTc 402-423 ms, axis about +21 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; QTc is well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold, but this tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 (post-start ECG still outstanding).

Atrial fibrillation: P waves absent (pre-QRS correlation -0.08) with grossly irregular RR intervals (560-1164 ms) and a mean ventricular rate of about 70 bpm. QRS 84 ms, QT about 420-446 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 455 ms using the mean RR (489 ms using the median RR), axis about +29 degrees, no bundle branch block, PR not measurable. The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12, pre-operative) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 168 ms and QTc about 399-409 ms, so this tracing shows NEW_AF (post-cardiac-surgery, with monitored AF entries on 2024-11-13 to 2024-11-15). The QTc rise is 48 ms on a mean-RR basis, below the 60 ms change threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, P wave before every QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 423-433 ms with Bazett QTc 416-427 ms, axis about +60 degrees. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG the day before (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62 bpm, QTc 450 ms) is essentially unchanged (QTc difference about 35 ms). This is the most recent tracing available; haloperidol was started 2026-09-15 and the post-start ECG is not yet due.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 347-349 ms with Bazett QTc 409-412 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76-77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT about 415 ms with Bazett QTc 469 ms (borderline prolonged), axis about +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with diffusely inverted T waves and QT about 470 ms, QTc about 524 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 55 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, so no change flag is recorded.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, P wave before each QRS with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, no AV block), QRS 90 ms, QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 395 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG (106186980, 2016-09-16: sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (-6 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 54-55 bpm with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, QT 403 ms with Bazett QTc 384 ms, axis about +4 degrees. The prior ECG (103042067, 2024-11-30) was sinus rhythm at 51 bpm with PR about 186-198 ms and QTc 365-367 ms; the QTc change is under 60 ms and there was no bundle branch block then either, so no change flags apply (the PR prolongation is at most marginally new and first-degree AV block is not a listed change).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no P waves (pre-QRS correlation -0.06), irregularly irregular RR 312-604 ms, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. QRS 100 ms, QT 265-268 ms with Bazett QTc about 415-426 ms, axis about -21 degrees, no bundle branch block, PR not measurable. The prior ECG the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with QTc about 421-424 ms, so this is NEW_AF (post-operative day 2 after cardiac surgery, with monitored AF entries 2025-09-13 to 2025-09-15). The QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 357-361 ms with Bazett QTc 395-399 ms, axis about +12 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) showed sinus rhythm at 68-70 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of 510-512 ms and QTc 542-544 ms; the QTc has fallen by nearly 150 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). The clinic note of 2026-11-23 describing sinus rhythm agrees with this tracing.
Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 178 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 387-389 ms with Bazett QTc 429-432 ms, axis about +55 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis about +47 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is markedly prolonged at 489-494 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 522 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms with QTc 360 ms at 75 bpm, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). The patient has been on escitalopram since 2024-05-14; this tracing is his most recent and meets the clinic threshold (QTc >= 500 ms) for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with regular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.01) and a consistent P wave before each QRS, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 287-297 ms with Bazett QTc 408-422 ms, axis about +65 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 317-324 ms with Bazett QTc 412-421 ms, axis about +58 degrees, no conduction block. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (100 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QTc 405-416 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 168 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 419-437 ms which corrects to a Bazett QTc of 389-405 ms at this slow rate, axis about +35 degrees. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22: sinus rhythm 57 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 354-394 ms) the rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change is well under 60 ms. Despite a history of atrial fibrillation (on warfarin) this tracing shows sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm (RR 492-496 ms, regular), PR about 130 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms, QT 289-293 ms with Bazett QTc 411-417 ms. The frontal axis is rightward (net QRS negative in lead I, slightly positive in aVF, about +160 degrees). Limb-lead voltages are small and the precordial R waves are poor. The prior ECG from earlier the same day (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall late R wave in V1 (peak at 112 ms) and terminal S waves in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block, with QTc about 480-491 ms; the block is no longer present (RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK) and the QTc has fallen by about 65-75 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60), much of which follows from loss of the wide QRS.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 170 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis about +67 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is prolonged at 527-531 ms with a Bazett QTc of 535-539 ms. The previous ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) had QT 475 ms at 47-49 bpm giving QTc 421-428 ms, so the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. This is the ECG obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement and it meets the QTc >= 500 ms threshold for prescriber review.

Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.21) with an irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 386-1070 ms, mean ventricular rate about 103 bpm. QRS 78 ms, QT 315-325 ms with Bazett QTc about 412-420 ms, frontal axis about -46 degrees (left axis deviation). No PR interval is measurable in the absence of P waves and there is no bundle branch block. Recorded the day after cardiac surgery (2024-09-17); monitored rhythm entries the same admission also show AF. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 292-294 ms with Bazett QTc 398-401 ms, axis about +34 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG (102955795, 2022-07-04: sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 394-395 ms) is unchanged. Despite a coded history of atrial flutter/fibrillation, all of this patient's tracings (2016-2023) show sinus rhythm; he remains on apixaban.

Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02) with a consistent low-amplitude P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.93, PR about 178 ms); no pacing spikes are present despite the pacemaker in situ. items.explanation: 71-year-old man (dob 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-08-22 cardiac surgery admission (Condition 7010d0e5) and carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note since, including the most recent visit 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference 174a63cd). Needs prescriber review to start anticoagulation; prior post-procedural hemorrhage (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an absolute contraindication.

Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the chart needs correction (she is anticoagulated on warfarin, but rate control and the AF documentation need review).

items.explanation: 71-year-old man (dob 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-08-22 cardiac surgery admission (Condition 7010d0e5) and carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note since, including the most recent visit 2026-07-28 (DocumentReference 174a63cd). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery = vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS class 1, score >=2 in men). Needs prescriber review to start anticoagulation; prior post-procedural hemorrhage (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an absolute contraindication.

On citalopram 40 mg daily continuously since 2023-10-02 (current order 7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order cbe91d0f, the first escitalopram order in the chart). ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QTc about 474 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold), so the requirement is met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order 88943096, first escitalopram order in the chart). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a; it first appears on that visit's medication list - the only earlier exposure was a brief inpatient course ending 2026-01-01). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a; the only earlier exposure was inpatient in 2024). That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264; it first appears on that visit's medication list, earlier haloperidol having been inpatient in Feb-Mar 2025). Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change by a clinic clinician, so under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. Nguyen PharmD): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist acting under the standing order, so an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. Anticoagulation is class 1 recommended for AF with prior stroke; needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia and documented falls from 2025-03 should be considered but do not preclude treatment). Her single ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

80-year-old woman (dob 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every Cardiology Clinic note from 2025-09-12 through the most recent visit 2026-05-28 (DocumentReference 5116e8ae ... a41e9ebb), and continuous monitored AF during the 2025-01-11 to 2025-01-20 admission (Heart Rhythm observations dee1f439 through 2558914f, 2025-01-17 to 2025-01-20). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis in AF; oral anticoagulation is class 1 recommended and needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg twice daily (current order dc397aff, 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28; the prior order 9bf97267 of 2026-06-30 also still runs to 2026-10-05). Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note instead states 'continue current regimen' and re-issued apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel, i.e. triple therapy) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. Anticoagulation is continuing despite a documented reason it should not continue without review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and both drugs appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with paroxysmal/persistent AF and CLL; one agent must be discontinued.

Per the QT monitoring memo this requires prescriber review; a repeat ECG is also warranted since the last tracing is nearly 3 years old.

No bundle branch block or AV block. Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm with a consistent P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.95), PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 335-367 ms with Bazett QTc 439-482 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no conduction block. Sinus tachycardia at 108-109 bpm, regular, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 338 ms with Bazett QTc 457 ms (mildly prolonged, partly an artefact of Bazett correction at this rate), axis about +41 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with regular RR intervals (864-882 ms) and a low-amplitude but consistent P wave, PR about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 398-417 ms with Bazett QTc 426-446 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 97-98 bpm, PR about 108 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 306-312 ms with Bazett QTc 390-397 ms, axis about -1 degree (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 367-385 ms with Bazett QTc 402-423 ms, axis about +21 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; QTc is well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold, but this tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 (post-start ECG still outstanding).

Atrial fibrillation: P waves absent (pre-QRS correlation -0.08) with grossly irregular RR intervals (560-1164 ms) and a mean ventricular rate of about 70 bpm. Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, P wave before every QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 423-433 ms with Bazett QTc 416-427 ms, axis about +60 degrees. No bundle branch block. This is the most recent tracing available; haloperidol was started 2026-09-15 and the post-start ECG is not yet due.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 347-349 ms with Bazett QTc 409-412 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76-77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT about 415 ms with Bazett QTc 469 ms (borderline prolonged), axis about +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with diffusely inverted T waves and QT about 470 ms, QTc about 524 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 55 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, so no change flag is recorded.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, P wave before each QRS with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, no AV block), QRS 90 ms, QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 395 ms, axis about +52 degrees. No conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG (106186980, 2016-09-16: sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 401 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (-6 ms).

The QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 357-361 ms with Bazett QTc 395-399 ms, axis about +12 degrees, no conduction block. The clinic note of 2026-11-23 describing sinus rhythm agrees with this tracing.
Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 178 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 387-389 ms with Bazett QTc 429-432 ms, axis about +55 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 292-294 ms with Bazett QTc 398-401 ms, axis about +34 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG (102955795, 2022-07-04: sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 394-395 ms) is unchanged. Despite a coded history of atrial flutter/fibrillation, all of this patient's tracings (2016-2023) show sinus rhythm; he remains on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one premature beat and a compensatory pause (RR 964, 986, 560, 1368, then 954-986 ms); the underlying rhythm is regular with a consistent P wave, PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block, QT 397-400 ms with Bazett QTc 403-407 ms, frontal axis about -32 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation (net QRS negative in II, III and aVF). Recorded on the day of her embolic stroke admission (2025-03-14); no atrial fibrillation is captured on this 10-second tracing even though paroxysmal AF was diagnosed during that admission. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (regular RR 838-884 ms) with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS, PR about 140 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 356-360 ms with Bazett QTc 383-387 ms. The frontal axis measures about -173 degrees (extreme): lead I and II are deeply negative while aVR is positive and the precordial leads are normal, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70-71 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is prolonged at 506-514 ms with a Bazett QTc of 547-555 ms. The prior ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QT 300-304 ms and QTc 446-451 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 100 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60) while on citalopram 40 mg daily; this meets the clinic threshold for prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis about +58 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T waves are inverted in I, V5 and V6 with a low-amplitude late positive deflection; QT measures about 445-448 ms (Bazett QTc 474-478 ms) taking the end of the T wave in the lead where it is latest, and about 405 ms (QTc 432 ms) if measured on lead I alone. Either way the QTc is below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This is the ECG obtained after escitalopram was started on 2026-02-12 and is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 54-66 bpm (sinus beats at RR 1110-1160 ms) interrupted by premature beats/couplets (RR 480-660 ms); P waves are consistent before the sinus beats with PR about 174 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 395-397 ms with Bazett QTc 374-376 ms using the dominant RR, axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG (108651109, 2018-12-13) was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR about 210 ms and QTc 391-394 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc are essentially unchanged (no AF on either tracing).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis about +47 degrees, no bundle branch block. The QT is markedly prolonged at 489-494 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 522 ms. The previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms with QTc 360 ms at 75 bpm, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). The patient has been on escitalopram since 2024-05-14; this tracing is his most recent and meets the clinic threshold (QTc >= 500 ms) for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02) with a consistent low-amplitude P wave before each QRS (P correlation 0.93, PR about 178 ms); no pacing spikes are present despite the pacemaker in situ.
